as Head of Shanghai Liaison Office of No. 10 Division
of the National Army (陸軍第十師駐滬連絡處 )
and assumed charge at No. 25 Yu Yuen Ch'un Villa, Yu
Yuen Road, the old premises of the Office on the 16th
inst. Apart from notifying parties concerned and of-
ficial organs of the Friendly Nation for record and
liaison purposes, the Police Department, S.M.C., is
requested to note and give directions and render as-
sistance when asked for.

Provisionally organized 13th Division of the
Nanking Government Army - Shanghai Office
closed.

The Shanghai office of the Provisionally
organized 13th Division of the Nanking Government Army
located at House 9 West End Gardens, Yu Yuen Road, U.C.I.,
has ceased functioning. Col. TAO SIH SUNG (陶雪生)
who was in charge of the office in question has been
appointed Commissioner of the 7th District Railway Guards
with the headquarters at 8 Yu-Ling Road (滬閔路),
U.C.I. The guards are said to have reorganized from
the Western District Self-Defence Corps, and are
responsible for the protection of the railway line and
its immediate vicinity between Tsipao (七寶) and
Singchuang (莘莊) along the Shanghai-Hangchow Railway.
They are under the direct control of the Mine Detachment
(峯部隊) of the Shanghai Garrison Headquarters.

December 25, 1941.

Provisionally Organized 13th Division - transfer.

According to information received, the
Provisionally Organized 13th Division of the Nanking
Government Army which is under the command of
TING SIH SAN (丁錫山) with divisional Headquarters
at Pei Jao (北橋), Minghong, has been ordered by
the Military Affairs Committee of the Nanking
Government to move its headquarters and troops now
stationed between Shanghai, Sungkiang & Fengking (楓涇)
along the Shanghai-Hangchow Railway, to Kashing at the
end of this month.

The cause of transfer of the division in
question is learned to be on account of the bad dicipline
of the men, as unlawful activities involving these
troops have frequently take place in the suburbs of.
Shanghai. Hence, in order to maintain peace and
order in Shanghai, the Japanese Military Authorities have
decided to move the division away from the Shanghai area.

1941年12月25日。

暂编第十三师——调动。

据收到的消息，由丁锡山（TING SIH SAN (丁錫山)）指挥、师部设在闵行北桥（Pei Jao (北橋)）的南京政府军暂编第十三师，已接到南京政府军事委员会命令，将于本月底将其师部及目前驻扎在沪杭铁路上海、松江及枫泾（Fengking (楓涇)）之间的部队调往嘉兴。

据悉，该师调动的原因是由于军纪败坏，涉及这些部队的非法活动在上海郊区频繁发生。因此，为了维持上海的治安秩序，日本军方当局决定将该师调离上海地区。

My name is ... u Yue Sung, age 48, native of Nuning,
Kiangsu, residing at 15 ... oo Foh ..., Fonquin Road. I was born
in my native place and came to Shanghai at the age of 20.
I made my living by working as a coolie in building yards and
pulling rickshas. Two years ago, my health ran down and I
changed my profession and became a vegetable hawker. Since
January 1939 I worked as a coolie on the coal boats on the
Bund where I made friends with another coolie named Tsang Ah
Kyung ( 張阿金 ). During the acquaintance the friend asked
me if I wished to get a job as cook in the Kiangsu-Chekiang
Suppression Committee with a monthly pay of $16.00. On my
answering in the affirmative, he took me to the Pao An ( 寶安 )

( 宋定洪 ) and vice captain Ho Kan Tsai ( 何幹才 ). There are
some 8 or 9 persons in the office and I heard that they had
9 pistols - descriptions of which are unknown to me as they
were always wrapped in newspaper.

This office is said to be branch of the "Li Kung Kwan"
at 76 Jessfield Road and is under the charge of Foo Ta Pao
( 傅世寶 ) and Lieu Ta Ching ( 劉大慶 ). At about 6 p.m.
11/10/39 Sung Ting Hung and Ho Kan Tsai took a parcel, contain-
ing the nine pistols (which I learned from the other inmates)
to "Li Kung Kwan". At about 5 p.m. on 12/10/39 a representa-
tive from "Li Kung Kwan" came to the office and summoned the
two captains to go there. Later, news was received to the

我叫……赵友松（... u Yue Sung），48岁，江苏南京人，居住在梵皇渡路15号……（... oo Foh ...）。我出生于原籍，20岁时来到上海。我以在建筑工地做苦力和拉人力车为生。两年前，我的健康状况恶化，便改了行，成为了一名蔬菜小贩。自1939年1月以来，我在外滩的煤船上做苦力，在那里我与另一名名叫张阿金（Tsang Ah Kyung）的苦力成了朋友。在相识期间，这位朋友问我是否愿意在江苏浙江肃清委员会谋得一份厨师的工作，月薪16.00美元。在我给予肯定答复后，他于1939年10月8日上午带我去了昌平路姚兆坊的宝安殓房（Pao An Coffin Repository），在那里我被介绍给宋定洪队长的私人秘书李粹（Lieu Sui）以及副队长何干才。办公室里有大约八九个人，我听说他们有9支手枪——由于这些手枪总是用报纸包裹着，我不了解其具体特征。

My name is Loo Ming (陸明), age 29, native of Funing,
Kiangsu Province. I was formerly a straw-dealer in Chapei
and following the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese Hostilities
I returned to my native place. During the early part of
June, 1939, I came to Shanghai and resided at an unnumbered
hut, off Singapore Road where I established the Sing Sung
Yuan (新盛園) Teashop. About two months ago, one of my
friends named Koo Tsoong Woo (郭崇和), whom I met in Chapei
during a business transaction when he was a boatman, approached
me and advised me to become a member of the Kiangsu-Chekiang
Suppression Committee at 1 Kong Ka Jao, off Connaught Road,
O.O.L. where he is a captain. He pointed out that it is very
difficult for me to run the teashop if I am not a member of the
organization. I was allowed to stay in my shop and to pay
occasional visits to the organization and to draw $20.00 per
month as wages. There were seven or eight other men in the
place and I did not know any of them with the exception of Koo
Tsoong Woo, who is the chief of the place, and one member named
Yangchow Siau Er Ts (揚州小二子) who always brought my pay to
my shop. Koo told me that the establishment at Kong Ka Jao
was a branch office of the "Li Kung Kwan", 76 Jessfield Road.
I only went to the place twice and no work was ever assigned to
me. All the inmates wear civilian clothes and as far I know
three mauser pistols were borrowed by Koo from "Li Kung Kwan"
and kept in his office. I have seen these pistols myself.
For the past three weeks, the 1st accused named Zau Yue
Sung has patronised my shop and become friendly with me.

我叫陆明（Loo Ming），29岁，江苏省阜宁县人。我以前是闸北的草席商人，中日战事爆发后，我回到了原籍。1939年6月初，我来到上海，居住在新加坡路旁一间无门牌号的棚屋里，并在那里开设了新盛园茶馆。大约两个月前，我在闸北做生意时认识的一位名叫郭崇和（Koo Tsoong Woo）的朋友找到我，当时他是一名船夫，他劝我加入位于外白渡桥康纳路旁孔家角1号的江苏浙江肃清委员会，他是那里的队长。他指出，如果我不是该组织的成员，我就很难经营茶馆。我被允许留在我的店里，偶尔去组织报到，并每月领取20.00美元的工资。那里还有七八个人，除了作为该处负责人的郭崇和，以及一名总是把我的薪水送到店里的名叫扬州小二子（Yangchow Siau Er Ts）的成员外，我不认识其他人。郭告诉我，孔家角的机构是杰斯菲尔德路76号“立功馆”的一个分部。我只去过那里两次，从未被分配过工作。所有在场人员都穿便服，据我所知，郭从“立功馆”借了三支毛瑟手枪，并保存在他的办公室里。我自己见过这些手枪。在过去三周里，第一被告赵友松常来光顾我的茶馆，并与我变得熟络。

The following is the statement of Wong Kung Pao (王根宝).
native of Funing. taken by me Daniel. Tuo Keng Yong.
translated
at Gendarme on the 21/10, 39. and interpreted by Clerk,

My name is Wong Kung Pao (王根宝), alias Siau Moh Ts
(小毛子), age 18, native of Funing, Kiangsu. I was born
in my native place and came to Shanghai with my parents at the
age of four. At the age of nine I worked as an apprentice
in the Chih Hsin (致新) glass works on Tsong Chin Road,
Chapel where I remained until I was 13. I then proceeded to
Yangpu where I worked for four months in a glass works and then
returned to Shanghai, where I worked in the Fung Ung (工友)
glass works, Fukang Road, Chapel. After the outbreak of the
hostilities I was unemployed and hawked cigarettes near the
clock tower on Robison Road. Sometime during the month of
April 1938 I got a job in the Fung Yue (工友) Glass Works
on Gordon Road near Napei Road but I was paid off on the 3rd
day of the 8th moon 1939. I stayed idle at home and loitered
about the roadway and one month ago I made the acquaintance of
1st accused named Lu Yue Sung (趙月生) who used to invite
me to go to his room in the Sih Dan (臺) lodging house,
101 Kong M. Jao, off Jessfield Road, O.O.L. (on east lease to
Joss House Road).
On his learning that I was unemployed, he promised to
seek a job for me at his place of employment,- the Kiangsu and
Chekiang Apprehension Committee which was to open at the Pao An
(宝安) Coffin Repository, Yue Chow Fang off Chungping Road
wherein he was employed as a cook.

On 10/10/39 he took me to the above place where I was
assigned the position of a teaboy with wages of 60 cents per day.
There are about 20 persons in the place and I know only the two
men to whom I dully attended namely:- Sung Ting Hang (宋鼎亨).

我叫王根宝（Wong Kung Pao），别名小毛子（Siau Moh Ts），18岁，江苏阜宁人。我出生于原籍，四岁时随父母来到上海。九岁时，我在 Chapel 区宗金路（Tsong Chin Road）的致新玻璃厂当学徒，一直做到十三岁。随后我去了杨浦，在一家玻璃厂工作了四个月，然后回到上海，在 Chapel 区福康路的工友玻璃厂工作。战事爆发后，我失业了，便在罗宾森路钟楼附近兜售香烟。1938年4月的某个时候，我在靠近纳皮尔路（Napei Road）的戈登路工友玻璃厂找到了一份工作，但在1939年农历八月初三被解雇。我闲居在家，在街上闲逛，一个月前我认识了第一被告赵月生（Lu Yue Sung，注：此处原文拼音与中文名对应可能有误，结合上下文应为赵友生/赵友松），他常邀请我去他在外白渡桥杰斯菲尔德路旁孔家角101号（东租界至庙街）的锡台（Sih Dan）旅馆的房间。
当他得知我失业后，他答应在他工作的地方为我找份工作——即江苏浙江缉捕委员会，该委员会将在昌平路姚兆坊的宝安殓房开业，他在那里受雇为厨师。

1939年10月10日，他带我去了上述地方，我被分配担任茶役，日薪60分。那里大约有20个人，我只认识我日常伺候的两个人，即：宋鼎亨（Sung Ting Hang）。

(1) 赵发生（Zau Yue Sung），48岁，广东籍，男/苦力，住通肯路伍福里15号。
(2) 李广友（Li Kwong Yue），28岁，广东籍，男/理发师，住彭南路220号。
(3) 路铭（Loo Ming），29岁，广东籍，男/店主，住新加坡路外越界筑路区无门牌棚屋。

搜查队成员观察到这五名嫌疑犯沿延平路走近，当搜查队准备对他们进行搜查时，这五名嫌疑犯企图沿延平路逃跑。搜查队成员随即追赶，并在延平路成功将他们逮捕。

During the morning of 15-10-39, several workmen
employed a electricians, joiners etc., visited the
locality and requested permission to remove certain

bridge. The request was refused.

Acting on instructions from Mr. Yorke, D.O."B" Div.,
the undersigned in company with Supt. Yao Chia Jui and
some twenty more uniform police and detectives visited
the premises at 11.45 a.m. 16-10-39, and conducted a

abandoned by the illegal occupants. However a large
quantity of property was seized (see attached lists)
and at 12.50 p.m. 16-10-39, was removed to Gordon Road
Police Station at the request of the Pao An Co.Officials.

While conversing with persons on the premises of the
Pao An Co., it was ascertained that on various dates
prior to the posting of the Search-parties, several
persons had been 'arrested' and detained in the illegal
occupied premises; among them being one Chinese female.

Two rooms were found to be in process of having
wooden-floors installed and workmen stated they under-
stood this portion was for 'Detention' rooms. Just out-
side said rooms, was a desk and two chairs which appeared
to have acted as the 'Office'. Several rooms showed signs
of very recent installation of lights, fittings & repairs.
On the North side of the premises a means of escape was
discovered. Being in the form of a table with a ladder
on top which just reached the top of the boundary-wall.
Persons leaving by this 'exit' were O.O.L.
